theme: Quellbrook Freight reference estate, operator web front end: a React + Vite single-page application (orders, order detail with shipment status, dispatch board) served by nginx behind the gateway; owned by the Edge team. Its plants are accessibility defects a team without automated accessibility checks ships.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Each row of the orders table opens the order on click (onClick on the <tr>), but the row is not focusable and has no key handler and no link inside it: keyboard and switch users cannot open an order from the list at all (WCAG 2.1.1).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The orders search box has a placeholder but no <label>, aria-label or aria-labelledby; the placeholder disappears on input and is not a reliable accessible name (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The dispatch board shows each route's vehicle as an icon image (van or rigid truck) with no alt attribute; the vehicle kind is information the operator needs (heavy express parcels need a rigid vehicle) and is not given anywhere else on the card (WCAG 1.1.1).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The header's divider image is decorative: alt="" and aria-hidden mark it so on purpose, and the brand name is in the text beside it.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The dispatch board's consignment filter has no visible <label> element but an aria-label that names it; a visible heading above the list says what it filters. It has an accessible name.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The board's compact/comfortable density preference is kept in localStorage. It is a display preference, not personal data or a token.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The cancel-order dialog is a native <dialog> opened with showModal(); its click handler closes it when the backdrop is clicked. Keyboard users close it with Escape (native) or its Close button; the click handler is a pointer convenience, not the only way.
